result.title: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
result.summary: Observational causal discovery often leaves causal di- rections unresolved or unstable. Large language mod- els (LLMs) can provide semantic information to resolve these directions, but incorrect proposals can exclude the true causal graph and invalidate downstream inference. We study three separate decisions: where to allocate semantic queries, which proposals to admit, and which causal graphs to retain. Our framework distinguishes population non-identifiability from finite-sample insta- bility, evaluates semantic orientation against statistical and random controls, and examines calibrated admis- sion and error-tolerant DAG retention. Experiments across benchmark networks show that semantic infor- mation improves recovery over coin-flip orientations, but targeting unstable edges has no established ad- vantage over matched-random allocation. The tested admission certificate cannot support nontrivial admis- sion with the available calibration tasks. Moreover, downstream retention depends on reference adequacy: learned references contain the true DAG in only three of 80 planned tasks. These findings separate the value of semantic information from the reliability of its alloca- tion, admission, and retention, and identify calibration size and reference adequacy as key limitations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在部分不可识别的因果发现中，LLM 语义先验应在何处查询、哪些候选方向可被接纳、哪些因果图应保留，并用统计与随机对照分离语义信息价值与其分配、接纳、保留环节的可靠性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「查询预算分配—校准接纳—容错保留」三决策与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、动态获取证据及 STOP 决策问题结构相似，且报告了定向分配不优于匹配随机分配，可供核查证据选择策略的收益来源。
